clue.text: Burn with energy for new blockade

indicators.note: X for Y means one letter takes the place of another in the word

parts.note: to singe is to burn lightly
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A fuel or fire is lit with vigour to start a fresh blockade.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with energy for new' tells you to put E where N stood in SINGE.
explanation.definitionFit: A siege is a military blockade of a town or fortress to force its surrender.

clue.text: Fake writer about golf discovered in confusion

parts.note: a sham is a fake

indicators.note: about means around, so the pen goes around the letters

parts.note: Bic is a brand of ballpoint pen, a writer

indicators.note: discovered means with the cover taken off, so the outer letters go

explanation.surface: A forger of writing about golf has been found out amid chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' means stripped of its cover, so take the outside letters off golf; Bic is a ballpoint pen brand, hence 'writer'.
explanation.definitionFit: Shambolic is informal for chaotic or disorganised.

clue.text: Complex trade involves accessory

indicators.note: involves means contains, so the letters lie within the words

explanation.surface: An elaborate business deal brings in an accomplice.
explanation.definitionFit: An extra is an additional item, an add-on or accessory.

clue.text: Undermining love at home, receiving nothing

parts.note: Eros is the Greek god of love

indicators.note: receiving means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: in means at home
O is the figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A romance at home is being sabotaged while gaining nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: Erosion is the gradual wearing away or weakening of something, as a cliff is undermined.

clue.text: Clear old platform

parts.note: manifest as an adjective means clear or obvious

explanation.surface: An instruction to clear away an old stage or political platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A party's platform is its published set of policies, which is what a manifesto declares.

clue.text: Thin silver with simple surrounding

indicators.note: surrounding means going around, so the first word encloses the second

parts.note: mere means simple or nothing more than
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A slender piece of silver in a plain setting.
explanation.definitionFit: Meagre means scanty or lean, which is a sense of thin.

clue.text: Pad dead tree edition perhaps?

definitions.meaning: a pad is a block of writing paper
a printed copy is, read in two parts, not an e-book: a cryptic second sense of the answer

explanation.surface: A writing pad might be called the paper version of something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dead tree edition' is jokey slang for a printed book; split the answer NOT EBOOK.
explanation.definitionFit: A pad is a block of paper for writing on, which is a notebook.

clue.text: Using every effort to fault supply

indicators.note: read as supple-y, supply means in a supple, bendy way, so the letters are bent into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone straining hard to find a flaw in the stock of goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supply' is not the noun but the adverb from supple.
explanation.definitionFit: Flat out means at full speed or with maximum effort.

clue.text: Nine roots developed into neurotransmitter

indicators.note: developed means grown or changed, so the letters take a new form

explanation.surface: Nine roots of a plant have grown into a brain chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: Serotonin is a chemical messenger that carries signals between nerve cells.

clue.text: Proprietor in depression, heading off

indicators.note: heading off means the head, the first letter, is removed

parts.note: a downer is slang for a depressing experience or low mood

explanation.surface: A shop owner who is feeling low, going away.
explanation.definitionFit: An owner is a proprietor, the person something belongs to.

clue.text: One needing space to work

parts.note: reads like someone wanting elbow room in an office, but the space is outer space

explanation.surface: Someone who needs plenty of room before they can get on with their job.
explanation.definitionFit: A space traveller's workplace is literally outer space, so they need space to work.

clue.text: Location for planes in minor park to the west

indicators.note: to the west says the hidden letters are read backwards
in says the letters are found inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Directions to where light aircraft are kept, in a small park off to the west.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters sit across 'minor park'; 'to the west' in an across clue means read right to left.
explanation.definitionFit: The apron is the paved area of an airfield where aircraft are parked, loaded and refuelled.

clue.text: Manufactured bizarre cooker

indicators.note: something manufactured is made up from raw materials, so the letters are put together afresh

explanation.surface: A factory has turned out an oddly designed stove.
explanation.definitionFit: A brazier is a metal container holding burning coals, used for heating or grilling food outdoors.

clue.text: Disapprove of plant denying a second jab

parts.note: to boo someone is to show loud disapproval

indicators.note: denying the word a means that letter is refused a place, so it is taken out

parts.note: an aster is a daisy-like garden plant

explanation.surface: An anti-vaccine voice objecting to a factory that refuses to give a second dose.
explanation.definitionFit: A booster is a follow-up vaccination given to renew immunity after the first course.

clue.text: Settled a bit of long list

parts.note: lit is a past tense of light, as a bird lit (settled) on a branch
any can mean at all or a bit, as in 'is it any better?'

explanation.surface: Someone has decided on a part of a lengthy list.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a tedious recital or lengthy enumeration, from the repetitive form of prayer.

clue.text: Time philosopher makes collection for union

parts.note: Jean-Jacques Rousseau was an 18th-century philosopher

explanation.surface: A thinker takes his time to assemble a coalition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trousseau is the clothes and linen a bride gathers for her marriage.

clue.text: Book's list of chapters literally inconsistent

parts.note: split it as in-cons-is-tent: the word tent is literally in the word cons

explanation.surface: A table of chapters that, taken at face value, doesn't match up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' asks you to read 'inconsistent' as a statement: TENT sits inside CONS, giving CON(TENT)S.
explanation.definitionFit: The contents page of a book sets out its chapters in order.

clue.text: Arranged soccer draw right away? It can't be criticised

indicators.note: arranged means put in order, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A rigged football draw with the right team absent: no one dares object.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arranged' rearranges SOCCER DRAW once R is taken 'away'.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an idea or institution treated as above criticism.

clue.text: Critical as musical knowledge shown up

indicators.note: shown up in a down clue means the letters read upwards, backwards

parts.note: Evita is the Lloyd Webber musical
gen is British slang for information or knowledge

explanation.surface: A harsh review because a show's lore was exposed.
explanation.definitionFit: Negative here means unfavourable or disapproving, as a critical review is.

clue.text: Team declared support for game controller

indicators.note: declared means spoken out, so the letters are what the words sound like

parts.note: a crew is a team, as of rowers
a pier is a support for a bridge or jetty

explanation.surface: A sports side announced its backing for the official in charge of a match.
explanation.definitionFit: A croupier runs a gaming table in a casino, dealing cards or spinning the wheel.

clue.text: Stink after job provides ineffective remedy

indicators.note: after means the smell comes second

parts.note: a place is a job or position
BO, body odour, is a stink

explanation.surface: A bad smell follows the work, and the treatment doesn't help.
explanation.definitionFit: A placebo is a dummy treatment with no active ingredient.

clue.text: Kings escaping from select prison is easy undertaking

indicators.note: the kings escape from the words, so those letters leave them

parts.note: to pick is to select
nick is British slang for a prison or police station
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king, so two kings are KK

explanation.surface: Royal prisoners breaking out of an exclusive jail find it easy work.
explanation.walkthrough: NICK is everyday British slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling something a picnic, as in 'no picnic', means it is an easy task.

clue.text: The setter's going around South American bottleneck

indicators.note: going around means surrounding, so the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: the setter is, from the setter's viewpoint, I'M
STH is an abbreviation for south
US means American

explanation.surface: A crossword setter travelling round South America to a narrow pass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The setter's' is a contraction of 'the setter is', so I'M; 'South American' looks like one phrase but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: An isthmus is a narrow neck of land, a geographical bottleneck.

clue.text: Split internally, putsch is miscarrying

indicators.note: internally means within, so the letters sit inside the words

explanation.surface: The coup has failed because of a division in the ranks.
explanation.definitionFit: A schism is a split or division, especially within a church or party.

clue.text: African people mostly accepting vehicle colouring

indicators.note: accepting means taking in, so one word goes around the other
mostly means most of the word, so its final letter goes

parts.note: the Masai are a people of Kenya and Tanzania
a car is a vehicle

explanation.surface: An African people, by and large, taking in a car's paint job.
explanation.definitionFit: Mascara is cosmetic colouring applied to the eyelashes.

clue.text: Bit of music popular and current in 2000

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the first pieces go within the Roman numerals

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for 1000, so 2000 is MM
in means fashionable or popular
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A trendy tune that was all the rage at the millennium.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note, a half note lasting two beats.

clue.text: Set bed by lake

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
Erie is one of the North American Great Lakes

explanation.surface: Instructions to put a bed down beside a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A coterie is a small exclusive group of people, a set or clique.

clue.text: Turner starts to rise once Temeraire overshadows rivals

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letter of each following word is used

explanation.surface: The painter Turner's reputation rises once his Fighting Temeraire eclipses the competition.
explanation.walkthrough: Turner's 'The Fighting Temeraire' is a famous painting; here a turner is something that turns.
explanation.definitionFit: A rotor is the rotating part of a machine, so it is something that turns.

clue.text: Delightful housing European relative

indicators.note: housing means giving a home to, so one word holds the other

parts.note: nice means pleasant or delightful

explanation.surface: A charming continental relation is putting someone up.
explanation.definitionFit: A niece is a family relation, the daughter of one's sibling.

clue.text: Foolish to arrest graduate with a peculiar style

indicators.note: to arrest is to seize and hold, so the first word holds the second

parts.note: idiotic means foolish
MA, Master of Arts, is a graduate

explanation.surface: A silly decision to detain a graduate who has an odd way of doing things.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatic language has the distinctive character of a particular writer, language or dialect.

clue.text: Gold floor inside quiet gloomy place

indicators.note: inside means the first pieces go within the last

parts.note: mum means silent, as in 'keep mum'
Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the sole of an oven or furnace is its floor

explanation.surface: A golden floor set within a hushed, sombre building.
explanation.definitionFit: A mausoleum is a grand tomb, a sombre building that houses the dead.

clue.text: Katherine perhaps is wise shunning diamonds

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so that letter is left out

parts.note: shrewd means astute or wise
D is the card abbreviation for diamonds

explanation.surface: A woman named Katherine is clever enough to avoid jewellery.
explanation.walkthrough: Katherine is the heroine of Shakespeare's The Taming of the Shrew.
explanation.definitionFit: A shrew is a bad-tempered woman, and Shakespeare's Katherine is the classic example.
